candidates.title: Symmetric cobalt-linked adduct screen
candidates.purpose: Screen whether TEA versus TEOA under matched P01 conditions gives donor-specific operando substrate-associated signals that are cobalt-dependent and CO2-origin-bounded on both donor sides, while limiting conclusions to descriptive donor-linked differences unless orthogonal assignment succeeds.
candidates.source_to_proposal: GX011 motivates a transferable possibility that TEOA can enter catalyst-associated adduct chemistry, but only in a Re system. EV004 and EV068 support operando state-sensitive measurements to compare catalyst-state changes with intermediate-related signals. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and altered active species can mimic catalyst-linked behavior, requiring no-cobalt and dark controls. EV080 and GX008 support isotopic and orthogonal assignment controls. This proposal transfers control logic and measurement strategy, not a proven Co mechanism.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor comparison. If substrate-associated observables differ while the chosen cobalt-sensitive observables remain similar, that supports donor-specific substrate/intermediate chemistry without requiring a distinct cobalt state. If both classes differ, donor effects may include cobalt speciation changes.

Tests whether TEOA-associated features require cobalt. A feature seen only with cobalt supports a catalyst-linked interpretation but does not by itself distinguish cobalt-linked from amine-linked CO2-derived structure.
TEA analogue of the cobalt-dependence test. Comparing this pair with the TEOA pair bounds whether cobalt dependence is donor-specific or general background behavior.
Tests whether TEOA features are light-dependent operating-state signals rather than dark pre-equilibria.
TEA-side analogue of the light-dependence test so the donor comparison is bounded symmetrically.
Assignment control for TEOA. A reproducible isotope-sensitive shift in a donor-specific feature supports CO2-derived character; absence of a shift weakens a CO2-derived assignment for that feature.
Assignment control for TEA. This mirrors the TEOA isotope arm so donor-specific CO2-derived assignment is bounded on both donor sides.

procedure: Prepare source-verified matched P01 samples and controls, varying only the listed factors and documenting reactor, gas handling, optical cell geometry, and background materials.

Run a pilot to preselect one cobalt-sensitive method that gives reproducible signals under the same operando configuration as IR; if none is viable, continue as an IR-only descriptive screen and narrow inference accordingly.
Collect during-reaction operando IR and the preselected cobalt-sensitive measurements for all groups with matched blanks and baseline handling.
Use the 13CO2 groups only to test assignment of selected donor-specific operando features and require agreement with cobalt-dependence or light-dependence before calling a feature catalyst-linked.

Report separate bounded conclusions for donor dependence, cobalt dependence, light dependence, and isotope sensitivity; do not infer a unique intermediate identity from one spectral feature or one method.
measurements: Operando IR features in regions plausibly associated with CO2-derived, carbonate-like, bicarbonate-like, amine-associated, or metal-associated species, interpreted only against matched no-cobalt, dark, and isotope controls.

One preselected cobalt-sensitive operando observable indicating donor-correlated changes in cobalt oxidation state or coordination environment; useful for state comparison but insufficient alone for intermediate assignment.
Feature persistence or loss in no-cobalt controls to distinguish catalyst-linked behavior from donor/background bands.
Feature persistence or loss in dark controls to distinguish operating-state signals from dark pre-equilibria.
Isotope-sensitive shifts or non-shifts in selected donor-specific features under 13CO2 to bound CO2-derived character on both donor sides.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA/TEOA difference in operando substrate-associated observables under matched conditions, with at least one donor-specific feature showing cobalt dependence or donor-correlated cobalt-state change and isotope behavior consistent with CO2-derived origin on the relevant donor side.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be no reproducible donor-specific operando difference after matched controls, or donor-specific signals that are fully reproduced without cobalt and lack isotope support or cobalt-state correlation, making cobalt-linked or donor-specific CO2-adduct chemistry unnecessary.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include unresolved spectral overlap, donor-dependent background absorption, failure of the chosen cobalt-sensitive method to resolve state differences, or isotope tests too weak for assignment. Such outcomes may still justify descriptive reporting of similarities or differences without mechanistic assignment.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not assume spectral windows, concentrations, or irradiation settings from unrelated systems. Use source-verified P01 settings if available; otherwise run a pilot with identical cell geometry, gas delivery, and background subtraction across groups. Advance a cobalt-sensitive method only if it can be collected reproducibly for both donors under the same sampling configuration; otherwise restrict the card to IR-based descriptive screening.
candidates.limitations: Direct Co-bpy evidence for TEA/TEOA adduct chemistry is absent in the supplied record. Heterogeneous background from g-C3N4 and mixed media may obscure weak bands. Even symmetric isotope controls do not cleanly distinguish amine-linked from cobalt-linked CO2-derived structures. No-cobalt controls alter the coordination environment, so they support but do not prove catalyst-linked assignment.
